sections.hypothesis: Holding a coin and shorting its perpetual future in equal size, while recent funding is positive, collects funding worth more than its costs and more than a stablecoin yield, with little price risk. Hypothetical: Kestrel can't short (P5 parked; retail shorting in Australia is CFDs at 2:1, real perps are wholesale-only). A pass is recorded as needs-shorting and never traded until a licensed retail route exists and Luke has checked the Swyftx employee trading policy. It needs a real perp: a CFD pays financing instead of funding.
sections.rationale: Who pays: leveraged longs. Perp funding is what traders who want leveraged long exposure pay to those who take the other side; in crypto that demand has mostly been long, so funding has mostly been positive. Outside evidence: crypto carry is large and time-varying, highest when speculative demand is (Schmeling, Schrimpf and Todorov 2023, BIS working paper 'Crypto carry'), and perp-spot arbitrage returns (He, Manela, Ross and von Wachter 2022, 'Fundamentals of perpetual futures'). Both to check before freezing. Not a rejected family: it isn't a price bet at all. Disclosed: findings 14 used funding as a price signal (and it failed); this collects it instead. Runs: one, one trial.
sections.rules: Each of BTC, ETH, SOL gets a third of equity. Each Sunday close, for each coin: if its mean funding rate over the last 7 days (21 settlements) was above zero, hold the hedge for the week: spot long S and perp short S, S = 2/3 of its third (the rest is the perp's margin at 2:1); otherwise that third is cash. Earns every funding settlement while held (a positive rate pays the short). Price moves are assumed to cancel (spot against perp); the basis isn't modelled (perp price history isn't stored for these coins): disclosed. If a day's high reaches 1.45x the week's entry, the perp short is margin-called: both legs close that day and pay a round trip, flagged. 2020-01-01 to 2025-10-31; nothing from the holdout.
sections.parameters: 7-day funding lookback, entry above zero, weekly, equal thirds, 2:1 margin. Nothing else is tried.
sections.costs: Each time a hedge opens or closes: the spot leg as kestrel.toml (7.5 bps plus the half-spread band) and the perp leg at 5 bps taker (an assumption to check) plus the same band, so about 4 fees and 4 half-spreads per round trip. Funding from Binance's archive. No borrow cost (a perp needs none).
